articles.summary: An attacker's first move is mapping your employees' public exposure. Most companies have never run that map on themselves.
articles.title: Someone Already Mapped Your People. It Wasn't You.

articles.summary: Exposure tells you who can be hit. Assessment tells you which attack is running against your industry right now, and who to test first.
articles.title: It Already Hit Your Sector. You're Next in Line.

articles.summary: The unit that fails isn't a person, it's a workflow, exposed by a moment on the calendar and a campaign aimed at your sector. Two of those three signals change every week.
articles.title: Your Company Made This Week's Shortlist

articles.summary: The quarterly phishing test rewards spotting a tell, which is the wrong skill. A real test runs the live attack, aimed at a specific person and workflow, on the channels it uses, and finds where the process breaks under pressure.
articles.title: Run the Attack Before They Do

articles.summary: Annual training still passes audits, but the attacks that matter now break processes, not quiz scores.
articles.title: The Death of Security Awareness
